topic.name: 4.3 Sustainable Production of Goods and Services

parts.problem_md:
**Extract:**

**SunnyShade Hats (SSH)**

SunnyShade Hats is a private limited company (Ltd) that designs and makes sun hats. It started six years ago and now has 40 production workers and 8 office staff in City M. SSH sells hats on its website and to independent clothes shops. The owners, Naila and Amir, want to expand by launching a new eco-friendly range called OceanWave.

SSH currently buys most fabric from Country T and pays in US dollars (USD). Fabric prices have been stable, but transport costs are rising. The company uses industrial sewing machines. A bank loan of £300 000 was used last year to buy new machines.

Quality is very important. Recent checks show defect rates have increased as new staff have joined. SSH plans to hire 20 more machinists. Managers are deciding how to motivate staff to increase output and reduce defects. Two ideas are:

- Piece rate (a payment per hat made)
- Job rotation with extra skills training

SSH is also reviewing its packaging for online orders. The current plastic mailer is cheap and waterproof. A supplier has offered recyclable cardboard packaging that looks premium but costs more and may be less water-resistant.

To support decision making, the finance manager prepared weekly cost data and a summary of assets and liabilities for this year and last year. The marketing team has created a simple online advert for the OceanWave launch. A news article has also highlighted changes in the economy that could affect SSH.

### Appendix 1 – Online advert (draft)

**SUNNYSHADE – OCEANWAVE**
Light • durable • **made from recycled fibres**
Intro price: **£24.99**
Free head-size guide • Free returns
Follow us @SunnyShadeHats

### Appendix 2 – Statement of financial position items (end of year)

| **Item** | **2025 (£)** | **2026 (£)** |
|---|---|---|
| Inventories | 120,000 | 90,000 |
| Trade receivables | 180,000 | 210,000 |
| Cash | 40,000 | 10,000 |
| Trade payables | 160,000 | 190,000 |
| Bank overdraft | 0 | 50,000 |
| Bank loan (long term) | 300,000 | 300,000 |

### Appendix 3 – Business news (extract)

The economy is facing mixed news this month. The local currency has dropped 8% against the US dollar since January, making imports more expensive. At the same time, the government announced a 5% rise in the minimum wage to help workers cope with higher living costs. Meanwhile, the central bank cut interest rates by one percentage point in a bid to boost economic growth and encourage more borrowing and investment.

### Appendix 4 – Weekly cost and output (current line)

| **Measure** | **Value** |
|---|---|
| Output (hats per week) | 3,000 |
| Fixed costs per week | £6,000 |
| Total variable costs per week | £15,000 |

SSH is thinking of switching to recyclable cardboard packaging for online orders. Explain two advantages and two disadvantages of this change for SSH.

Refer to the following [insert](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2025/09/37160_Paper%202%20Set%20A%20Insert.pdf) when answering the question.
parts.solution_md:
Recyclable cardboard strengthens the eco brand image **[K] **and matches OceanWave’s “made from recycled fibres” promise in the advert, which can increase conversion at £24.99 among eco-aware online buyers **[Ap]**

Cardboard can provide a premium unboxing experience **[K] **that is easy to promote via @SunnyShadeHats and customer reviews, which can build loyalty and word-of-mouth for the launch **[Ap]**

However, cardboard is often more expensive and less water-resistant than the current plastic mailer **[K]**, so damaged parcels and returns may rise, increasing fulfilment cost and risking lower star-ratings for online orders **[Ap]**

Additionally, cardboard is typically bulkier and heavier to store and ship **[K]**, so postage and warehouse space costs could increase unless SSH redesigns pack sizes or negotiates new rates with couriers **[Ap]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - In your answer:
> 
>   - Give four valid points related to the question → 4 K marks
>   - Explain each point by clearly linking to the case study  → 4 Ap marks
> - Give a maximum of  2 advantages and 2 disadvantages
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - Relevant points might include:
> 
>   - Advantages
>   
>     - Eco-friendly packaging aligns with OceanWave’s sustainability message [k], so customers who value the environment may be more willing to purchase at £24.99 [ap], improving online conversion and supporting the launch positioning [an]
>     - A premium cardboard pack can enhance the unboxing experience [k], which SSH can showcase on social media via @SunnyShadeHats [ap] to generate positive reviews and repeat buying for the new range [an]
>     - Recyclable packaging can reduce reputational risk from plastic use [k], meaning SSH may receive fewer negative comments about waste and ethics [ap] on its website and platforms, supporting brand trust [an]
>   - Disadvantages
>   
>     - Cardboard can be bulkier/heavier to store and ship [k], so postage charges and warehouse space [ap] needs may rise, which reduces contribution per order unless SSH raises price or optimises pack design [an]
>     - Supply reliability and lead times for new packaging must be managed [k], because late packaging deliveries would delay dispatches, harming delivery times and customer satisfaction [an] during the OceanWave launch [ap]

**Extract:**

**Furniture Outdoors (FO)**

FO has been a private limited company for 20 years. It is owned and run by the Chan family and is located in country Z. In country Z the secondary sector has become relatively more important as the country has developed. FO is a manufacturer of wooden furniture that is suitable for outdoor use. Its products include tables, chairs and other outdoor furniture.

Customers order online from the FO website. The furniture is then delivered to customers in country Z using FO’s own delivery vehicles. However, FO is considering changing to selling its furniture through either wholesalers or large retailers in country Z.

The Chan family have the business objective of contributing to sustainable development. FO only uses sustainably sourced wood when making furniture. This is from local forests in country Z and the wood is more expensive than imported alternatives.

For many years FO shareholders have reinvested profits to provide the finance for growth. FO recently took over 2 other furniture businesses in country Z and plans further takeovers. The Chan family plan to continue to control and manage FO after this expansion. The leadership style of these two companies is very different to that of FO and their factories are located several miles away from FO in different regions of country Z.

FO need to manage all its resources effectively. It tries to use the same components such as nails, brackets and paint for all its furniture designs. It is important to not run out of raw materials and so orders to suppliers must be carefully planned to avoid late deliveries. FO want to keep wastage of materials to a minimum. FO also need to consider how many employees are required to complete each order.

**Appendix 1 - FO website advertisement**

**FO - the only business to go to when you need new outdoor furniture for your garden. **

FO produce a range of high quality furniture to meet all your needs for fashionable, well designed outdoor furniture. Be reassured our furniture is only made from the highest quality wood from sustainable forests.

Our furniture is only available online so order today and have your furniture delivered in the next few weeks. Email any questions to us and we will reply quickly.

**Appendix 2**

**Extract of cost, selling price and sales data for one of FO’s products**

| **Fixed cost per month** | \$10 000 |
|---|---|
| **Variable cost per table** | \$125 |
| **Selling price per table** | \$250 |
| **Forecasts sales for tables per month** | 100 |

**Appendix 3 **

**Newspaper article from the Daily News April 2021 **

**Sustainable production needed to save the planet **

A report from the International Committee for the Planet states that manufacturers must find more sustainable ways to produce their products as global warming is becoming more of an issue.

The report suggests three main ways manufacturers can change:

- Only use raw materials from sources that replace what they have used. This is estimated to raise variable costs by 20%
- Only use packaging that can be recycled. Costs are estimated to increase but the selling price may not rise by more than 10%
- Only use electric vehicles to deliver products. The cost of buying electric vehicles is more than petrol or diesel vehicles. Using electric vehicles could enable variable costs to be reduced by 5%.

Consider the following **three** sustainable production methods FO could implement:

- use renewable energy sources (solar panels) to power all manufacturing equipment
- implement a zero-waste production system where all wood offcuts are recycled into smaller products
- adopt lean manufacturing techniques to reduce material waste by 30%.

Which production method should FO choose to maximise profit? **Justify** your answer.

Refer to the following [insert ](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2024/09/0450-june-2021-insert-paper-2-cie-igcse-business---new.pdf)when answering the question.
parts.solution_md:
Using renewable energy sources (solar panels) would align with FO's sustainability objectives and create a strong environmental reputation **[Ap]**. However, the initial investment cost would be approximately £50,000 for solar panel installation **[Ap]**, which would take several years to recover through reduced electricity costs **[An]**

Implementing a zero-waste production system would utilise all wood offcuts currently discarded **[Ap]**. This could generate additional revenue streams from smaller products whilst reducing raw material costs by up to 15% **[Ap]**. The system would enhance FO's eco-friendly brand image and appeal to environmentally conscious customers **[An]**

Adopting lean manufacturing techniques would reduce material waste by 30%, lowering variable costs per table by approximately £18.75 **[Ap]**. This method requires minimal initial investment but demands staff training and process restructuring **[Ap]**. The cost savings would directly improve profit margins on each unit sold **[An]**

To maximise profit, FO should choose to implement lean manufacturing techniques **[E]**. This option provides immediate cost reductions with minimal upfront investment, directly improving profitability **[Ap]**. Unlike solar panels which require substantial capital outlay, lean manufacturing delivers quick returns through reduced waste and lower production costs **[E]**. While zero-waste systems offer potential, lean manufacturing provides guaranteed cost savings that will enhance FO's competitiveness in the furniture market **[E]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> **Structure**
> 
> - Write one PEA paragraph for each production method identified in the question:
> 
>   - Point: Identify the production method
>   - Evidence (Ap): Apply case study detail
>   - Analysis (An): Explain business impact
>   - Add a final Evaluation (E):
>   
>     - Decide which method is most profitable
>     - Justify your choice
>     - Compare and reject alternatives
> 
> **Marking approach**
> 
> - This is a levelled response answer in which the examiner determines how well you have demonstrated skills of application, analysis and evaluation
> 
>   - Application (4) – Use case study facts
>   - Analysis (4) – Chain effects clearly, using business terms
>   - Evaluation (4) – Balanced judgement, rejects others with reasoning
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - **Use renewable energy sources (solar panels)**
> 
>   - **Advantages**
>   
>     - Creates strong environmental credentials → attracts sustainability-focused customers
>     - Reduces long-term electricity costs → lower variable costs over time
>     - Differentiates FO from competitors → potential premium pricing
>   - **Disadvantages**
>   
>     - High initial investment of £50,000 → significant capital requirement
>     - Long payback period → delayed return on investment
> - **Implement zero-waste production system**
> 
>   - **Advantages**
>   
>     - Utilises all wood materials → reduces raw material costs by 15%
>     - Creates additional revenue streams → improves overall profitability
>     - Enhances eco-friendly reputation → attracts green consumers
>   - **Disadvantages**
>   
>     - Requires new production processes → operational complexity increases
>     - May need additional equipment → moderate investment required
> - **Adopt lean manufacturing techniques**
> 
>   - **Advantages**
>   
>     - Reduces material waste by 30% → saves £18.75 per table
>     - Minimal upfront investment → quick implementation possible
>     - Immediate cost savings → direct profit improvement
>   - **Disadvantages**
>   
>     - Requires staff training → temporary productivity disruption
>     - Process restructuring needed → management time investment
> - **Conclusion**
> 
>   - Solar panels offer long-term benefits but require substantial upfront investment with delayed returns
>   - Zero-waste systems provide cost savings and revenue opportunities but add operational complexity
>   - Lean manufacturing delivers immediate cost reductions with minimal investment requirements
>   - FO should prioritise lean manufacturing for maximum profit impact while considering other methods for future implementation

**Playsafe Playground Equipment (PPE)**

Kaari has always been creative and made wooden toys for her two children when they were young. Her children are now at school, so Kaari decided to start her own business making wooden playground equipment.

Kaari started PPE as a sole trader business three years ago in country Z. She wants an income from the business but also wants to spend time with her children. Kaari wants the business to remain small. However, if the business grows Kaari may need to change to another type of business organisation. Kaari carries out all the management roles in the business.

Kaari uses job production to produce high quality, individually designed playground equipment. Kaari designs all the equipment herself and she employs 3 skilled workers to help her make the products. PPE currently makes both large and small items of playground equipment each week.

Kaari uses cost-plus pricing as every item of playground equipment uses different quantities of raw materials. She sells small items of playground equipment to retailers and large items of playground equipment to the Government. There are many competitors in this market.

Kaari plans to obtain new machinery which will cost \$20 000. She is considering using crowd-funding as this is one way to raise capital for new business investment. Other options include leasing the machinery or asking the bank for a loan.

Kaari has developed a new unique product this year. There are no other similar products in the market.

**Appendix 1**

**Advertisement for PPE**

Buy your playground equipment from us.

At PPE we manufacture high quality playground equipment and have better designs than our competitors.

All our equipment has been fully tested and is guaranteed to meet legal safety standards. We are the main supplier of playground equipment to the Government for public parks - so you know our equipment can be trusted!

Contact us today for a price list.

**Appendix 2**

**Cost and revenue information for PPE in 2021**

|   | **Small item of playgroundequipment** | **Large item of playgroundequipment** |
|---|---|---|
| Average selling price | \$100 | \$1 000 |
| Average cost of manufacture | \$25 | \$500 |
| Output each week | 15 | 3 |

**Appendix 3**

**Newspaper article – Main News 1st October 2021**

**Children need to get more exercise and play outside**

Research suggests that playing outside helps children relax after school and improves their health.

The Government in country Z has allocated \$10m to spend on improving children’s playgrounds in public places. This means there will be \$5 000 to spend on equipment for each public playground.

Retailers have reported increasing demand for small items of playground equipment as parents want to have these products at home. This trend is expected to continue.

Consider the advantages and disadvantages to PPE of investing in the following **three** types of sustainable production technology to improve their manufacturing process:

- Solar-powered machinery
- Recycled material processing equipment
- Energy-efficient LED lighting systems

Which sustainable technology investment should PPE prioritise? **Justify** your answer.

Refer to the following[ insert](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2024/09/jun-2021-paper-2-case-study-v2---new.pdf) when answering the question.
parts.solution_md:
Solar-powered machinery would reduce PPE's electricity costs and carbon footprint for playground equipment production **[Ap]**, supporting environmental sustainability goals. However, the high initial installation cost of \$\$25,000 could strain cash flow **[Ap]**, and weather dependency may affect consistent power supply **[An]**

Recycled material processing equipment would enable PPE to use sustainable materials like recycled plastics and metals **[Ap]**, reducing raw material costs and appealing to environmentally conscious customers. This could differentiate PPE from competitors through eco-friendly playground equipment **[Ap]**. However, processing recycled materials may require quality testing and could initially slow production speeds **[An]**

Energy-efficient LED lighting systems would reduce electricity consumption by 60% compared to traditional lighting **[Ap]**, lowering operational costs and supporting sustainable manufacturing practices. The lighting would improve working conditions for the 3 employees **[Ap]**. However, LED systems have higher upfront costs than conventional lighting **[An]**, and may require electrical modifications to existing facilities **[An]**

PPE should prioritise recycled material processing equipment **[E]**. As consumer demand for sustainable products increases, eco-friendly playground equipment would provide competitive advantage **[Ap]** and justify premium pricing strategies **[E]**. Unlike solar panels or LED lighting, recycled material processing directly impacts product differentiation **[E]** and creates long-term cost savings through reduced raw material expenses **[E]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> **Structure**
> 
> - Write one PEA paragraph for each point identified in the question:
> 
>   - Point: Identify the sustainable technology benefit/drawback
>   - Evidence (Ap): Apply case study detail
>   - Analysis (An): Explain business impact
>   - Add a final Evaluation (E):
>   
>     - Decide which technology offers best return on investment
>     - Justify your choice
>     - Compare and reject alternatives
> 
> **Marking approach**
> 
> - This is a levelled response answer in which the examiner determines how well you have demonstrated skills of application, analysis and evaluation
> 
>   - Application (4) – Use case study facts
>   - Analysis (4) – Chain effects clearly, using business terms
>   - Evaluation (4) – Balanced judgement, rejects others with reasoning
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - **Solar-powered machinery**
> 
>   - **Advantages**
>   
>     - Reduced electricity costs → lower operational expenses
>     - Zero carbon emissions during operation → environmental sustainability
>     - Government incentives available → reduced payback period
>   - **Disadvantages**
>   
>     - High capital investment of \$\$25,000 → cash flow constraints
>     - Weather dependency → inconsistent power generation
>     - Maintenance requirements → ongoing operational costs
> - **Recycled material processing equipment**
> 
>   - **Advantages**
>   
>     - Lower raw material costs → improved profit margins
>     - Eco-friendly product positioning → competitive differentiation
>     - Waste reduction → environmental compliance benefits
>   - **Disadvantages**
>   
>     - Quality control challenges → potential product defects
>     - Processing time requirements → reduced production efficiency
>     - Supplier reliability issues → supply chain risks
> - **Energy-efficient LED lighting systems**
> 
>   - **Advantages**
>   
>     - 60% energy reduction → significant cost savings
>     - Improved working conditions → enhanced employee productivity
>     - Long lifespan → reduced replacement costs
>   - **Disadvantages**
>   
>     - Higher upfront investment → initial cash outlay
>     - Installation complexity → potential production disruption
>     - Technology updates → potential obsolescence risks
> - **Conclusion**
> 
>   - Recycled material processing offers direct product differentiation with growing market demand
>   - Solar machinery provides long-term savings but requires substantial upfront investment
>   - LED lighting improves efficiency but offers limited competitive advantage
>   - PPE should prioritise technology that maximises sustainable market positioning while managing financial constraints

parts.problem_md: Do you think it is always possible for a manufacturing business to reduce its resource use? **Justify** your answer.
parts.solution_md:
Manufacturing businesses can implement lean production techniques **[K]**, which eliminate waste and improve efficiency, leading to reduced material consumption and lower operating costs **[An]**

Businesses can also invest in modern technology and automation **[K]**, which can optimise resource usage and reduce material waste during production processes **[An]**

However, some manufacturing processes have minimum resource requirements that cannot be reduced without compromising product quality or safety standards **[K]**, which means businesses may face technical limitations that prevent further resource reduction **[An]**

For manufacturing businesses with sufficient capital and flexible production processes, reducing resource use is often achievable **[E]**. This allows them to lower costs whilst meeting environmental regulations and consumer expectations **[E]**

However, businesses operating with outdated equipment or producing highly regulated products may find it difficult to reduce resource use without significant investment. The feasibility ultimately depends on the industry sector, available technology, and regulatory constraints **[E]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - You are writing a mini-argument with a decision
> 
>   - Give one relevant reason to support your view → 1 K mark
>   - Explain why this reason helps the business (cause-effect chain) → 1 An mark
>   - Give a different possible reason or viewpoint → 1 K mark
>   - Explain why this could also help the business → 1 An mark
>   - Make a decision — which argument is stronger or more important overall? → up to 2 E marks
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - Points might include:
> 
>   - Recycling and reusing materials [k] reducing raw material requirements [an]
>   - Technical limitations in certain processes [k] preventing further resource reduction [an]
>   - High costs of upgrading equipment [k] making resource reduction financially unviable [an]
>   - Regulatory requirements [k]
>   - Automation and AI [k]
>   - Can optimise resource allocation and reduce waste [an]
> 
> - Justification might include:
> 
>   - Lean production reduces waste [k] which lowers material costs and improves efficiency [an].
>   - However, some processes have minimum resource requirements [k] which cannot be reduced without affecting quality [an]
>   - It might only be possible if the business has sufficient capital for investment [eval] and operates in an industry with flexible production requirements [eval]

parts.problem_md: Do you think sustainable production methods are the best approach for a manufacturing business to adopt? **Justify** your answer.
parts.solution_md:
Sustainable production methods help businesses reduce their environmental impact **[K]**, which can improve their brand reputation and attract environmentally conscious consumers, potentially increasing sales and market share **[An]**

Sustainable production can also lead to long-term cost savings through reduced waste and more efficient use of resources **[K]**, helping businesses lower their operating costs and improve profitability over time **[An]**

However, implementing sustainable production methods often requires significant upfront investment in new technology and equipment **[K]**, which may strain the business's cash flow and reduce short-term profits **[An]**

For manufacturing businesses operating in markets where consumers value environmental responsibility, sustainable production is likely the best approach **[E]**. It allows them to differentiate their products and build customer loyalty whilst reducing long-term costs **[E]**

However, for businesses with limited capital or operating in price-sensitive markets, traditional production methods may be more viable in the short term. The choice ultimately depends on the target market, available resources, and long-term business strategy **[E]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - You are writing a mini-argument with a decision
> 
>   - Give one relevant reason to support your view → 1 K mark
>   - Explain why this reason helps the business (cause-effect chain) → 1 An mark
>   - Give a different possible reason or viewpoint → 1 K mark
>   - Explain why this could also help the business → 1 An mark
>   - Make a decision — which argument is stronger or more important overall? → up to 2 E marks
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - Points might include:
> 
>   - More efficient use of resources [k] leading to lower operating costs [an]
>   - Meets regulatory requirements [k] avoiding fines/penalties [an]
>   - Access to green financing/grants [k] reducing capital costs [an]
>   - May increase production costs initially [k] reducing short-term profits [an]
>   - Limited consumer demand for sustainable products [k] may not justify higher costs [an]
>   - Traditional production methods [k]
>   - Lower initial costs/faster implementation [an]
>   - Lean production [k]
>   - Reduces waste whilst maintaining efficiency [an]
> 
> - Justification might include:
> 
>   - Sustainable production reduces environmental impact [k] which improves brand reputation and attracts environmentally conscious consumers [an].
>   - However, it requires significant upfront investment [k] which may strain the business's finances [an]
>   - It might only be worthwhile if there is sufficient consumer demand for sustainable products [eval] and the business can afford the initial costs [eval]

> **[case-study]**
> GreenCycle Manufacturing is a UK-based company that produces garden furniture from 100% recycled aluminium and plastic materials. The company has developed an innovative circular production model where all manufacturing waste is collected, reprocessed, and integrated back into new products. GreenCycle has invested £3.2m in state-of-the-art recycling technology and quality assurance systems. The facility processes 750 tonnes of recycled materials annually, transforming them into premium outdoor furniture collections. The operations manager stated: 'Our focus on reusing and recycling materials has created significant operational benefits, though it demands substantial investment in advanced processing capabilities and stringent quality management.'
